steps.message:
Marguerite has the resolution-basis item open on the Ocotillo peer-review checklist and will not sign Phase 1 rev B until it closes.  I need a short note I can put in front of her that settles the resolution question on what is already on the file server, because nothing new is being run for this.

Tell me where the plume resolution index lands for the result the report rests on, with the cell size and the plume length scale behind it, and whether our band is met.  Then tell me what our resolution acceptance rests on, and whether anything about that basis needs a decision from Marguerite.

I also want to know whether the resolved-energy figure was taken inside the region the index describes, and whether the ambient values behind the plume length scale represent the site, and what the site's conditions would do to it.

Last, tell me whether the item can close, and if it cannot, what would settle it.

Put it in a Word note saved as /filesystem/CFDME-2025-041_resolution_note_revA.docx please.

Para 27: style=Normal, text=  = 0.0775 × (10,040)^0.46
Para 28: style=Normal, text=  = 5.4 m
Para 29: style=Normal, text=L above is the wind-tilted Byram flame length; it is not a still-air buoyant flame height and is not comparable to Heskestad’s still-air correlation (see Section 5 for the idealization record).
Para 30: style=Normal, text=4.  Froude / Regime Assessment
Para 31: style=Normal, text=Regime selection follows CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §2. The controlling non-dimensional group is the Froude number formed on the characteristic source diameter of the LES sub-domain:
Para 32: style=Normal, text=Fr = u_wind / sqrt(g · D_char)
Para 33: style=Normal, text=Taking D_char = 3.0 m (the LES sub-domain segment fixed in Section 5 below) and g = 9.81 m/s²:
Para 34: style=Normal, text=sqrt(g · D_char) = sqrt(9.81 × 3.0) = sqrt(29.43) = 5.42 m/s
Para 35: style=Normal, text=Evaluated across the site design wind envelope 5–12 m/s:
Para 36: style=Normal, text=
Para 37: style=Normal, text=The Froude / plume-velocity ratio falls in the range ~0.9–2.2 across the entire design envelope.
Para 38: style=Normal, text=Regime classification.  Classification against the Modeling Standard §2 thresholds, and solver selection per §3 of that standard, shall be carried out and documented in the case setup record before any case in this matrix is meshed.
Para 39: style=Normal, text=This classification is made once, at the firm level, for the entire Phase 1 wildfire matrix; it is not re-argued case-by-case within the envelope.
Para 40: style=Normal, text=5.  LES Sub-Domain
Para 41: style=Normal, text=The LES sub-domain represents a 3.0 m segment of the flaming front. This segment length is the characteristic source width used for the plume model, and the value of D_char used in the Section 4 Froude computation and in the plume-length-scale computation below.
Para 42: style=Normal, text=5.1  Line vs Axisymmetric Reconciliation
Para 43: style=Normal, text=The Byram fireline-intensity relation of Section 3 gives an intensity per unit length of the fire front (kW/m). The plume length scale D* referred to by the firm modeling and verification standards is an axisymmetric-source property (kW total). The two quantities are not interchangeable and cannot be composed directly. The 3.0 m segment length is the specific conversion factor between them for this project: it defines how much fire-front length is captured within one LES sub-domain, and therefore what total heat release rate the plume model sees.
Para 44: style=Normal, text=Design fire heat release rate for the sub-domain:
Para 45: style=Normal, text=Q = I × L_segment
Para 46: style=Normal, text=  = (10,040 kW/m) × (3.0 m)
Para 47: style=Normal, text=  = 30,120 kW
Para 48: style=Normal, text=  = 30.1 MW
Para 49: style=Normal, text=Idealizations recorded so they are not misread as physical dimensions.
Para 50: style=Normal, text=•  Flame depth and flame residence time are not resolved in this sub-domain. The flaming front is represented as an equivalent 3.0 m characteristic-diameter source patch.
Para 51: style=Normal, text=•  The wind-tilted Byram flame length L = 5.4 m from Section 3 is a wind-tilted correlation length; it is not a still-air buoyant flame height. Heskestad’s still-air flame-height correlation, evaluated for the same 30.1 MW heat release rate at a 3.0 m diameter source, gives roughly 11.5 m. The 5.4 m vs 11.5 m gap between the two correlations is not treated as a discrepancy between two attempts to model the same quantity.
Para 52: style=Normal, text=Plume characteristic diameter D*.  For Q = 30.1 MW and standard reference-atmosphere conditions (ρ_∞ = 1.204 kg/m³, c_p = 1.005 kJ/kg·K, T_∞ = 293.15 K, g = 9.81 m/s²):
Para 53: style=Normal, text=D* = ( Q / ( rho_inf · c_p · T_inf · sqrt(g) ) )^(2/5)
Para 54: style=Normal, text=   = ( 30,100 / ( 1.204 × 1.005 × 293.15 × 3.132 ) )^(2/5)
Para 55: style=Normal, text=   = ( 27.08 )^(2/5)
Para 56: style=Normal, text=D* = 3.76 m.
Para 57: style=Normal, text=The fine-grid cell size specified for the LES mesh study is dx = 0.5 m (the finest of the three grids in the mesh study). This gives:
Para 58: style=Normal, text=D* / dx = 3.76 / 0.5 = 7.5
Para 59: style=Normal, text=which confirms the plume is adequately resolved on the fine grid. LES resolution acceptance shall be assessed per the firm QA standard applicable to reacting-plume LES.
Para 60: style=Normal, text=6.  Wall Assembly Note
Para 61: style=Normal, text=The through-wall response of the assembly cannot be modelled as heat conduction through a single solid slab. Per the OAS-WUI-01_revC wall assembly section (Geometry/OAS_wall_assembly_section.png), the assembly is a double-wythe cavity system: two 50 mm printed-concrete leaves separated by a 205 mm open-air cavity (overall thickness 305 mm), tied together by continuous 9-gauge (3.8 mm) galvanized truss-type steel ties spaced 600 mm on centre vertically, embedded 25 mm into each leaf. The cavity carries no insulation. The architectural drawing (OAS_wall_assembly_section.png) uses the drawing-side identifier OAS-WA-305mm-DW in its title block; this refers to the same physical wall assembly as the engineering geometry of record OAS-WUI-01_revC used throughout the SOW, this memo, and all downstream analysis artifacts.
Para 62: style=Normal, text=The metallic ties are a continuous parallel thermal path between the exposed and unexposed leaves; their conductivity (~45 W/m·K) is more than an order of magnitude above the siliceous-aggregate concrete of the leaves, and they are the reason the single-point criterion governs over the average-rise criterion in the ASTM E119 test result of record.
Para 63: style=Normal, text=Per CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §6, the through-wall modeling treatment for this assembly shall be selected and documented in the case setup record before meshing, accounting for the metallic ties’ thermal-bridge role identified above. Temperature-dependent solid properties (k, ρ, c_p) apply per Modeling Standard §3.5.
Para 64: style=Normal, text=7.  Downstream Inputs
Para 65: style=Normal, text=The following quantities established above are the source-term and length-scale inputs for the downstream Phase 1 case-setup, mesh-study, and reporting artifacts:
Para 66: style=Normal, text=•  Site design envelope: ambient 35–42 °C, RH 10–25 %, 20-ft wind 5–12 m/s (Section 2).
Para 67: style=Normal, text=•  Byram fireline intensity I = 10,040 kW/m (Section 3).
Para 68: style=Normal, text=•  Wind-tilted Byram flame length L = 5.4 m (Section 3).
Para 69: style=Normal, text=•  LES sub-domain fire-front segment: 3.0 m (Section 5).
Para 70: style=Normal, text=•  Design fire heat release rate: 30.1 MW (Section 5.1).
Para 71: style=Normal, text=•  Plume characteristic diameter: D* = 3.76 m (Section 5.1).
Para 72: style=Normal, text=•  Froude ratio range across the site design envelope: ~0.9–2.2 (Section 4); regime classification and solver selection per Modeling Standard §§2–3 to be documented in the case setup record (Section 4).
Para 73: style=Normal, text=•  Wall through-thickness modeling treatment: to be selected and documented per Modeling Standard §6, accounting for the metallic tie thermal-bridge path identified in Section 6.
Para 74: style=Normal, text=The 3.0 m segment, 30.1 MW source, and D* = 3.76 m established per Section 5 above are the inputs the fine grid dx = 0.5 m recorded in the Meshing and case-build log is sized against.
Para 75: style=Normal, text=The 5–12 m/s design wind envelope carries forward into the wind-inlet boundary conditions of the six-case matrix, per the solver selection made in Section 4; the puffing frequency of 0.87 Hz predicted by the f = 1.5·D^(-1/2) correlation per CFDME_Modeling_Standards_Fire_rev4.pdf §4 for this plume sets the writeInterval and end-time requirements for each transient run.
